candidates.evidence: Three in-plane modes at 102.8, 205.8 and 241.9 cm-1. The angular pattern shows an Ag-type diagonal tensor for the 103 and 242 modes and a B1g-type (xy) off-diagonal tensor for the 205 mode, which fits an orthorhombic layered chalcogenide with the beam along the layer normal. The ~100 and ~240 cm-1 positions are close to GeS literature values as I recall them (not verified in this session); the 205 cm-1 mode does not match a recalled GeS mode clearly.
Same orthorhombic symmetry class allows the same Ag/B1g pattern. Recalled GeSe mode positions were not checked against these three peaks in a verifiable way, so this is a weak alternative.
Same orthorhombic symmetry class. Recalled SnS mode positions do not obviously include a ~240 cm-1 Raman line, so this is a low-confidence alternative.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was supplied (material_hint null), so nothing was checked against a stated material. The identification rests only on the three peak positions, their widths and their angular (Raman-tensor) patterns. The directory name was not used as evidence. The assignments to GeS come from recalled literature values, which I could not verify in this session.

peaks.assignment: A_g-type in-plane diagonal mode; candidate GeS low-frequency A_g mode (recalled ~96-98 cm-1, not verified)
peaks.source: Measured position and FWHM from a global Lorentzian fit (shared shape, +/-0.05 cm-1). Angular fit: parallel = k(A+R cos2θ')^2 with A/R~1.1 (180-periodic dominant, 4θ harmonic ~1/4 of 2θ); crossed = k R^2 sin^2(2θ') (90-periodic, max ~1900, min ~0). Mixed pattern matches no single category. Irrep from symmetry reasoning: diagonal in-plane tensor for backscatter along the layer normal gives A_g.

peaks.assignment: B_1g-type in-plane off-diagonal (xy) mode; candidate GeS B-type mode (recalled ~185-215 cm-1, not verified)
peaks.source: Measured angular fit: parallel ~ 7290[1+cos(4θ-33 deg)] ~ cos^2(2(θ-8 deg)), crossed ~ 7330[1-cos(4θ-33 deg)] ~ sin^2(2(θ-8 deg)); parallel+crossed constant at ~14,600 counts across all angles. Axes are 45 deg from the A_g axes, so the tensor is off-diagonal, i.e. B_1g (xy) by symmetry reasoning.

peaks.assignment: A_g-type in-plane diagonal mode; candidate GeS A_g near 240-245 cm-1 (recalled, not verified)
peaks.source: Measured angular fit: parallel is 180-periodic (2θ harmonic ~4600 counts, 4θ ~300 counts; max near 53 deg, min near 143 deg); crossed is weak and nonzero (mean ~230 +/- 50 counts, modulated ~250 counts), so not isotropic_par_only. Same common axis as the 103 cm-1 mode, with A/R~4 (near-isotropic diagonal tensor). Irrep from symmetry reasoning.

properties.name: phase
properties.source: Symmetry pattern of three modes (two A_g-type diagonal, one B_1g-type off-diagonal). Not unique; the frequencies do not confirm it.

properties.name: layers
properties.source: No interlayer or low-frequency mode was measured: the window starts at 60 cm-1. Bulk vs few-layer cannot be decided from this data.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.source: No extra peaks above noise in the 62-415 cm-1 scan; narrow peaks (FWHM 3.4-8.8 cm-1).

limits: Identification is tentative. Only three peaks are present, no thickness, temperature or reference spectrum is available, and the GeS frequencies are recalled from memory rather than checked against a source (no references were retrieved here). The 205 cm-1 mode is not clearly matched to any recalled GeS line. Confidence for GeS is at most about 0.45.
Layer number and bulk vs few-layer status cannot be determined from this data.

Irrep labels (A_g, B_1g) are symmetry inferences. They assume backscatter along a crystal axis (the layer normal), in-plane axes that are crystal axes, and an orthorhombic point group. The sample orientation relative to the lab zero is unknown. The fitted phases (~53 deg for the A_g modes, ~8 deg for the B mode) are reported as measured lab angles and are not matched to crystal axes.

Classification of 103 cm-1 as 'other' versus 242 cm-1 as 'twofold' depends on category thresholds. Both share the same common axis and A_g-type diagonal character, differing mainly in the ratio of isotropic to anisotropic amplitude (A/R ~1.1 vs ~4).

The crossed-configuration signal of the 242 cm-1 mode is weak (mean ~230 counts, about 4 sigma; per-point noise ~350 counts) and its modulation is near significance. Its angular pattern is anticorrelated with the 205 cm-1 crossed signal, which argues against a Lorentzian-tail leak from the 205 cm-1 peak, but the crossed 242 cm-1 result remains uncertain.

Lineshapes were assumed Lorentzian with widths shared across angles. No instrument resolution was given, so the FWHM values are apparent widths. Position uncertainties (+/-0.05 cm-1) are statistical only; wavenumber calibration is not stated.

Spectral window is 60-417 cm-1. Silicon at 520.7 cm-1 and higher-frequency modes were not in range; the metadata says the sample is suspended, so no substrate line is expected, but this was not checked.

A scan of additional Lorentzian features (1 cm-1 steps, 62-415 cm-1) found a best candidate at ~261 cm-1 in parallel (|t| ~3.9). Its per-angle amplitudes scatter randomly (-185 to +665 counts, per-angle error ~180) and it is not reproducible, so it is not reported as a peak. With ~350 trial positions this is consistent with noise.
No cosmic-ray spikes were found: no point deviated by more than 5 sigma from the per-spectrum fit residuals.
